chapter: Spirits of Rhythm and the road in the 1930s
title: Feeding the broke band; pot smoking and the fight with Doug
summary: Bunn passed the hat to feed the band, who smoked pot all night, and he split Doug's tiple in a fight in Buffalo.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: When did you start to -- were you getting studio work all along, like through the early '30s? You were working with the Spirits, but you were mostly in New York, right?
Yeah.
So you had opportunities to play a lot.
Yeah. I had opportunities to play, but most of the time I'd get dates, you know.
Uh-huh.
I'd get dates and go on and play and then nights when I didn't have to do nothing, I wanted to have some money, and the band got broke and everything, and I was around there feeding them.
Right.
I had to buy their food and I was going out at nights, making it passing my hat, you know.
Uh-huh.
And I'd come in with 15, 25, $30.00. And I split it up and bought the food and took care of them, in other words.
Uh-huh. They didn't do a very good job of taking care of themselves, it sounds like.
No, they was on that pot.
Uh-huh.
They was smoking that pot, man. Not that I didn't smoke any, too, you know.
Yeah.
But that was the biggest mistake. They'd get their money at nights and the man would come in with cans
right in Philadelphia, and bags full of pot and fill it up, where you live.
Oh, yeah?

And they'd sit down there all night long and roll it. The next day they'd go out and buy some more. Smoke it up and go out the next day and buy some more. I didn't use it too much. Whenever I felt like I wanted to feel good, you know, I'd get me a joint and go ahead and smoke it by myself. I wouldn't even have it with them.
Uh-huh.
Me and Doug had a fight in -- where's that place you said, going up north?
You mean In Buffalo?
Buffalo, New York.
Uh-huh.

Him and I got in a fight, and he hit at me with his tipple and split it, and I done this with my guitar and busted the side of his head open. He had no business messing with me in the first place. I told him, "I don't want to fight you. I don't want to argue with you." I said, "Let me alone." So he kept agitating. "When I got solos you come in and try to mess me around." And I said, "No, I don't." "Yes, you do." Bam, with his tipple. Because he was loaded, real loaded. I mean, he smoked pot, boy, like it was going out of style.
Yeah.
They'd get cans of it. Bags of it. You getting that on this?
Yeah. Yeah.
(Laughter)
It's all the truth, right?
Yeah, it's the truth. Nothing I could get along with without telling you the truth.
Yeah.
Because that's what happened. That's all you wanted, the truth.
